1.explanation: Prism’s VB/VB.NET grammars live in prism-visual-basic.js (and its minified counterpart) and in prism-vbnet.js (plus its minified file). These modules define how comments and line continuations are tokenized. Because the bug involves how the underscore ( _ ) at the end of a commented line is handled, the grammar rules in these files must be updated so that comments ending with a continuation character are treated as a single comment token across lines. The bundled prism.js will pick up these changes when rebuilt.
1.bug_scenario: In Visual Basic code, a comment that ends with the line-continuation character ( _ ) is not recognized as a single multi-line comment by Prism. The first line (starting with ') is highlighted correctly as a comment, but the second line (indented continuation) is parsed as code, so tokens like Title:= and Default:= are colored instead of remaining part of the comment.

2.explanation: Both files define the Visual Basic language grammar for Prism, including the regular expression rules for comments. The bug arises because the comment pattern in prism-visual-basic.js does not recognize line continuation (the trailing underscore) and thus does not treat the next line as part of the same comment. Updating the comment regex in prism-visual-basic.js (and rebuilding prism-visual-basic.min.js) is needed to support multi-line commented statements ending with an underscore.
2.bug_scenario: In Visual Basic you can continue a comment onto the next line by ending the commented line with a space and underscore (_). Prism’s Visual Basic grammar, however, only treats a comment as a single‐line token and doesn’t pick up the continuation lines. In the screenshot you can see the first line preceded by a single quote is highlighted correctly, but the continuation line (after the underscore) is not included in the comment token.
